Thanks Jenny — I see the W-9 and the bank letter. A few items needed from AP/legal before we can schedule the payment:

- Beneficial Owner Attestation: For our vendor onboarding policy, any corporate vendor exceeding cumulative $250k or with PO>50k requires a signed Beneficial Owner Attestation. Can you confirm whether Solus has a single owner or multiple beneficial owners and provide the signed attestation?
- Corporate registration: copy of Articles of Incorporation or equivalent (we'll keep on file).
- 1099 treatment: our system will flag corporate vendors as 1099-exempt, but we need the W-9 box 3/corporation confirmation to be clear in the vendor record. The signed W-9 you sent should be sufficient — we'll still need you to confirm if any of your subsidiaries will invoice Redwood from a non-corporate entity.
- PO: we'll include PO 74231 on the Redwood invoice — please confirm the invoice should be addressed to Solus Therapeutics, Inc. and that PO 74231 will appear on your side.

I am attaching our vendor_onboarding_checklist.pdf for your convenience. Once we have the attestation and articles, I can create the vendor in our AP system and target payment on 2026-11-30 (Net 30). If anything changes, I'll update the expected payment date.

Marissa / Aditya —

Couple of legal items to note for the vendor file (to avoid re-work later):

1) Beneficial owner attestation: If Solus signs the attestation but lists owners with <25% ownership each, that's fine. If there are any individual owners >25%, we should capture full name, DOB, SSN (or passport for non-US owners), and residential address (per BOI rules).

2) W-9 verification: Confirm that the W-9 is signed and that the business classification is indicated. If Solus is invoicing from a US corp, 1099-NEC is typically not required — but this is transaction-dependent (services vs. goods). If any future invoice is for non-employee compensation to an individual or single-member LLC taxed as sole proprietor, we need to revisit.

3) Payment routing: If Solus elects to receive payment via a third-party vendor (PayThru), we need an authorization letter from the company authorizing PayThru to receive funds on their behalf. Otherwise, proceed with direct ACH.

4) Retention: Keep copies of the W-9 and Articles in the vendor record; run a quarterly check if any tax classification changes.

I'll review the Beneficial_Owner_Attestation once received. If you want, I can provide a redlined template that only requests the minimum BOI fields to avoid sharing SSNs via email.

— Mina
Mina Haddad
